claim_scope: This append-only correction supersedes the force-reset blast-radius packet at commit d62432cca. It binds both valid and stale manifests to the selected output directory before restart or reset, introduces a versioned 128-bit Compose identity for newly generated manifests, derives teardown paths from the selected directory, and classifies then refuses automatic teardown of the collision-prone legacy 32-bit identity.
failure_modes: allow-invalid recovery passes an unrelated Compose project into teardown
a valid manifest generated for directory B is copied into directory A and bypasses fallback-only identity checks
two output directories collide in the retired 32-bit project namespace and one teardown addresses both
stale host paths redirect Compose parsing or volume declarations during teardown
hardening the force path prevents an operator from replacing an identity-bound stale manifest

aaa.reason: Tests arrange identity-bound stale manifests, a valid relocated manifest, an invalid identity, hostile path-bearing fields, and a concrete legacy collision pair; act through normal loading, force loading, and teardown construction; then assert recovery, rejection before effects, v2 separation, and trusted path derivation.

reject_is_noop.reason: Every manifest identity mismatch and every legacy project raises before engine detection, Compose teardown, filesystem removal, or fresh stack generation. An identity-bound v2 stale manifest reaches teardown only through a newly derived project and safe environment.

nonclaims: The committed force-reset blast-radius packet did not cover valid relocated manifests or the collision-prone 32-bit Compose namespace. This packet supersedes those claims without rewriting that historical packet.
The force-reset loader may return other identity-bound stale fields, but v2 teardown consumes no project, host path, rendered path, port, chain, network, or proof-mode value from them.
Legacy 32-bit manifests are not automatically migrated or torn down. Operator-assisted collision-safe migration remains unimplemented.
A 128-bit content-derived identity reduces practical collision risk; it is not a mathematical proof that distinct paths can never collide.
No executable semantic-mutation campaign was run, so mutation evidence is intentionally absent.
No settlement, proof, migration, writer-rotation, value-moving, or production authority is added.
